period: July 2020 to July 2021 (pus and body fluids: July 2020 to June 2021)
citation: Postgraduate Department of Microbiology, Government Medical College Srinagar. Antibiogram for the year July 2020 to 2021 (blood; pus and body fluids; urine). Srinagar: Government Medical College; 2021.
reporting: Percent susceptible. Blood: organism counts for NICU and for IPD and ICU, one Gram-negative table with the number of isolates (IPD, ICU and NICU together) and a Candida antifungal table. Pus and body fluids: one list of percentages per organism with its isolate number. Urine: one list of percentages per organism with its share of isolates only.

verification.note: Scanned PDF, read from page images (scanned PDF). Two separate readings of every table: pass 1 from whole pages rendered at scale 2.5, pass 2 from crops at scale 2.6 to 3 (landscape pages in halves). The two readings were compared by script: 256 of 256 values, isolate numbers and counts agreed; page 6 is a second scan of page 5 with the same values. No cell was unreadable.

notes: Antibiogram of the Postgraduate Department of Microbiology, GMC Srinagar, for July 2020 to July 2021 (cover letter dated 25 November 2021; the pus and body fluid section covers July 2020 to June 2021). Blood: the organism counts are printed separately for the NICU and for "IPD and ICU"; both are recorded as inpatient counts (NICU patients are inpatients), which the app adds up. The Gram-negative table's isolate numbers equal NICU plus IPD and ICU for E. coli (30), Klebsiella (89), Pseudomonas (39) and Acinetobacter (158), so it covers all blood cultures (IPD, ICU and NICU) and is recorded as all inpatients; Burkholderia is printed as 37 there but 32 in the counts. The Candida antifungal table (110 isolates, 39.4%) matches the NICU count (Candida 110) and the NICU chart (279 positive specimens; 110/279 = 39.4%), and the IPD and ICU counts list no Candida, so it is recorded as ICU (NICU). C. albicans 32 (29%), non-albicans 78 (71%); the report attributes the flucytosine resistance to C. krusei. The blood table's "Quinolones" column (a drug class) and the "Ceftazidime/tazobactam" and "Ticarcillin" entries of the pus lists have no drug key and are not recorded. Urine rows have no n (only each organism's share of isolates: E. coli 70%, Klebsiella 12%, Enterococcus 8%, P. aeruginosa 6%, S. aureus 2% with MRSA 30% and MSSA 70%, Acinetobacter 1%, Proteus 1%). Several pus Enterococcus percentages (11 isolates: vancomycin 93, ampicillin 48, penicillin 47) cannot be produced by 11 or fewer isolates (source error, recorded as printed).
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 184 cells (including the seeded 40% sample of 74), all 23 row n values and all 21 counts were read blind from the page images (scale 3 to 4.5, landscape pages in parts) and compared with the file by script: 0 differences, nothing corrected; page 6 re-read as a second scan of page 5 with the same values.

Blood Gram-negative table recorded as inpatient: supported. Its n equal the NICU plus the IPD and ICU counts of page 3 (E. coli 8 + 22 = 30, Klebsiella 19 + 70 = 89, Pseudomonas 0 + 39 = 39, Acinetobacter 34 + 124 = 158), and the whole-blood block of page 3 (3520 samples) is exactly IPD and ICU (3060) plus NICU (460), with no OPD block.

Candida antifungal row recorded as icu (NICU): supported. Its 110 isolates (39.4%) equal the NICU Candida count (110) and 110 of the 279 NICU positive specimens of the page 4 chart, and the IPD and ICU block lists no Candida.

Burkholderia count mismatch confirmed as printed: 37 isolates in the Gram-negative table (page 5 and its second scan, page 6) against 32 in the IPD and ICU counts (page 3) and the IPD chart (page 4), none in the NICU (a source inconsistency, already in the row note).

Cells not kept, re-read on page 9: pus Enterococcus (n=11) vancomycin 93, ampicillin 48, penicillin 47 (cautions) and gentamicin 52 (printed as plain "Gentamycin", intrinsic) are printed that way (source, not transcription). Pus, urine settings "all" (no location split) and specimens confirmed.
